The Prophet sends Jarir with 150 Ahmas riders to Dhul-Khalasa, an idol house called the Yemeni Ka'bah; he prays for Jarir to sit firm, and Jarir burns and dismantles it.
Abu Raja recalls worshipping stones and mounds of earth before Islam, removing spearheads in Rajab, and his people running to Musailima when they heard of the Prophet.
Bahira, Sa'iba, Wasila and Ham were camels dedicated to idols, and the Prophet saw Amr bin Amir Al-Khuza'i, who began the practice, dragging his intestines in the Fire.
Lat was a man who mixed sawiq for pilgrims; one who swears by Lat and Uzza must affirm Allah's oneness; reverence for Manat kept some from Safa and Marwa.
Idols named after pious men of Noah's people, set up at Satan's prompting and worshipped once their origin was forgotten, were later worshipped by Arabs: Wadd, Suwa', Yaghouth, Ya'uq, Nasr.
